title: Drag anchoring and filter-suggestion overlay for large tables
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a robust drag-anchoring model for column resizing combined with a contextual filter-suggestion overlay for high-cardinality virtualized tables. Goal: reduce accidental column collapse during fast drags, surface filter suggestions based on visible column content, and preserve density profile presets when users change column widths.
acceptance_criteria: Drag anchoring keeps adjacent columns from shifting unexpectedly when user performs quick drags; handoff animation provides clear visual feedback.
Filter-suggestion overlay appears on column header press or via keyboard shortcut and shows top 5 suggested filters computed client-side from visible rows (sampled) and offers 'create filter' CTA.
Density presets (Compact / Comfortable / Spacious) persist per-user and survive column width changes and virtualized row buffer adjustments.
Keyboard interaction: users can focus a header, press Space to open suggestion overlay, Tab to navigate suggestions, Enter to apply.
Performance: no measurable increase >5% in frame drop or scroll jank on large datasets (100k rows with virtualization); overlay render fast-path off main thread where possible.
Accessibility: overlay is announced by screen readers, has ARIA roles/labels, and meets WCAG focus order expectations.
Telemetry: events emit for resize_start, resize_end, suggestion_view, suggestion_apply with minimal payload (headerKey, duration, appliedFilter).
Design review approval completed and at least one engineering spike PR linked for kernel of interaction logic.
engineering_considerations: Spike recommended to prototype pointer-event throttling and CSS transform-only animations to avoid layout thrash.
Virtualization buffer must be expanded transiently during drag to avoid placeholder blanks for adjacent columns; test with current continuous-batching rendering pipeline.
Filter suggestions should use a light-weight sampler that reads visible rows from KV cache snapshot where possible to avoid traversing full dataset.
Consider adding a small 'drag momentum' heuristic to determine when to lock anchoring (fast flicks vs deliberate drags).
Backend: no server changes required; suggestions are client/console-side. If customer datasets are large and sensitive, mark suggestion feature opt-in for Private deployments.

usability_notes: Recommendations from sessions: show 'more like this' filter chips at the top of overlay for common numeric ranges and categorical top values.
Users expect 'snap-to-width' when double-clicking the resize rail; implement snap to content width and to minimum widths for dense modes.
Avoid permanent overlays that obscure multi-column drag targets — overlay should be contextual and dismiss on scroll or drag begin.
design_decisions: Anchoring model: two modes — soft-anchor (default) with 120ms handoff animation, and hard-lock when user holds Shift to resize multi-column groups.
Suggestion overlay: transient, anchored to header with caret. Keyboard-first entry via Space/Enter. Data sampling limited to current render buffer.
Density persistence: store preset key in Console user preferences; column widths stored per-column per-preset to allow quick restore.
